bull_bear.body:
- **Winter dependence:** still 45% of revenue; weak winter / warm-winter season is the structural risk. Q1 structurally weak (~12–13% of annual revenue) due to winter returns.
- **Demand / macro:** petrol/diesel/LPG-driven inflation could defer discretionary apparel spend; geopolitical tension is the named overhang (reason guidance deferred to Q2).

- **Returns:** elevated at 17% of gross sales (up from 15%).
- **Solar execution:** highly leveraged (75% debt), commissioning/vendor finalization pending, IRR sensitivity; non-core distraction risk.
- **Export:** Middle East orders stalled on regional uncertainty.
- **Competition:** fast-fashion (Zara, Shein) — mgmt dismisses (present in India 10–15 yrs already; relies on own design USP + large market).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Confident and execution-focused. Repeatedly emphasized track record of meeting annual guidance (guided 15%, delivered 16%; ~20% EBITDA met). Deliberately conservative on FY27 quantitative guidance — explicitly deferred to Q2 citing geopolitical/oil uncertainty, while firmly committing to "double-digit growth." Notably more candid on energy diversification (Rishabh Oswal). Declines quarter-by-quarter guidance on principle (seasonality).
bull_bear.title: Management Tone

bull_bear.body:
- Margin beat driven by LOWER DISCOUNTS, not lower returns — returns actually ROSE to 17%. Investors initially assumed lower returns helped; mgmt corrected.
- Inventory won't structurally fall because shift to SIS/LFS/online means stock sits in channel partners' accounts (only end-sales recognized).
- Solar revenue (~INR 15–16 cr) is OVER AND ABOVE / outside the standalone apparel guidance — don't double-count.
- One-off FY26 store correction (~14–15 closures) masks underlying ~43 gross store adds; muddies the net-26 figure vs 40–45 guidance.
- Q1 is only ~12–13% of full-year revenue — a weak Q1 print is structural, not a red flag.
- Non-DCR solar modules: cheaper but forfeit the INR 1.05 cr/MW central CFA subsidy — net still accretive to IRR.

- Established brand equity and leadership position in the organised winterwear market, with the flagship Monte Carlo brand supported by differentiated sub-brands (Luxuria, Rock.it, Tweens, Cloak & Decker, Denim, Alpha, Monte Carlo Home)

bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Seasonal concentration in woollens — Woollen knitted garments have historically contributed a meaningful share of annual turnover concentrated in the third quarter of the financial year — in FY26 woollens accounted for 19.4% of Q4 segmental sales versus 27.7% for the full year. Diversification into cotton, cotton-blended apparel, home furnishings, kids' wear and footwear is expected only to gradually reduce this seasonal concentration over the coming years, so earnings remain skewed to the winter season.
- Input cost volatility, with a dated cliff on the cotton customs-duty relief — Profitability remains sensitive to raw material, power and other input costs. Cotton and synthetic fibre prices are volatile, driven by weather, global demand and policy shifts, while elevated energy and freight costs linked to the Middle East conflict add pressure. The current customs duty relief on cotton imports is temporary and scheduled to lapse on 31 October 2026 — ahead of the peak woollen and winter-season sourcing cycle, so costs could step up right at the seasonal build.
- Sustained industry-wide discounting pressuring realisations — Both domestic and international brands continue to lean on early discounts and sales promotions to drive walk-ins and defend market share, a trend the Company expects to persist. This structural discounting environment could keep pressure on realisations across branded apparel, including for Monte Carlo.
- Intensifying competition from foreign brands and fashion-cycle inventory risk — Continued entry of foreign brands into India has intensified competition and raised the cost of maintaining market visibility. Continuous product innovation is essential to stay ahead of fashion trends; failure to manage inventory effectively or track consumer tastes closely could leave unsold stock or force markdowns that hit margins.
- Execution risk in nascent categories — Scaling relatively new categories — footwear, athleisure and quick-commerce partnerships — carries execution risks distinct from the established cotton and woollen business: unfamiliar supply chains, different competitive dynamics and the risk of brand dilution if quality or positioning is not carefully managed. Replicating core-category execution standards will be important to sustaining the strong FY26 growth rates.
- Regulatory, legal and tax compliance risk, including the GST rate step-up on higher-priced garments — Changes in the regulatory and tax environment can increase costs, erode margins and affect cash flows, with potential fines or reputational damage for non-compliance. The Company specifically flags the evolving GST structure, under which garments above INR 2,500 now attract an 18% rate, up from 12% — a direct headwind for the premium end of its portfolio.
- Macro headwinds from slower global growth and elevated inflation — Moderated global growth and elevated inflation following the Middle East conflict, alongside continued global trade tension, could dampen discretionary consumer spending domestically and add cost pressure across freight and input costs beyond cotton specifically.
- Forward carbon border tax exposure as exports scale — Current carbon border tax regimes largely exclude finished garments and textiles, but the sector's high emissions intensity places it in a watch category for future regulatory expansion, with a second carbon border regime set to take effect from a major export market in the near term. Not an immediate cost, but a compliance risk worth monitoring as Monte Carlo scales exports.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Monte Carlo's expansion in FY26 was retail-footprint and channel led rather than plant led. The Company operates two state-of-the-art integrated manufacturing facilities in Ludhiana, Punjab (the Notice-of-AGM 'Works' listing names four Ludhiana sites: G.T. Road Sherpur; 231 Industrial Area-A; Plot No. 425 & 427 near Textile Colony; and B-XXX-1781/784, Old C-12, Phase V, Focal Point), supported by an in-house design team of 26+ professionals producing approximately 900 SKUs per month. It manufactures 100% of its woollen clothing and approximately 70% of its cotton garments in-house, with the remaining approximately 30% (home textiles, footwear and poly-blend products) outsourced to third-party manufacturers. As part of its FY27 growth strategy the Company plans to further modernise its manufacturing facilities and warehousing infrastructure and streamline business processes to support its expanding product portfolio. Retail expansion is the principal capacity build-out: during FY26 the network reached 497 Exclusive Brand Outlets (341 FOFO and 156 COCO), 1,615 Multi-Brand Outlets, 891 National Chain Store counters and 578 Shop-in-Shop/NCS outlets, with 26 net new EBOs added during the year. Going forward the Company intends to accelerate retail expansion through the asset-light FOFO model, targeting 40-45 Exclusive Brand Outlets annually (the Directors' Report states the addition of 40-50 new stores every year), while deepening North and East India and accelerating into the Southern and Western regions. New channels added in FY26 include entry into direct international e-commerce via the overseas platforms Joom.com and Stylishop.com, quick-commerce partnerships with Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto enabling deliveries within 30 minutes in select markets, and a strategic collaboration with Salesforce for digital transformation. On the corporate structure side the Company incorporated MCFL Energy Projects Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary on 19 January 2026 to undertake business in renewable energy and allied activities. No rupee capex quantum was disclosed: the capital-commitments named disclosure in this bundle carries only cross-references to note 34 and no figure.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural transformation of India's textile and apparel industry supported by strong domestic consumption, rising organised retail penetration, increasing digitalisation and expanding global sourcing opportunities
- Premiumisation of the Indian fashion market driven by rising disposable incomes, greater brand awareness and consumer preference for quality and differentiated product offerings; per Deloitte, the mid-premium band (INR 3,500-7,000) is projected to grow strongly and premium apparel faster still
- Shift towards branded and organised retail, omnichannel commerce and products offering greater comfort, functionality and sustainability, creating opportunities across apparel, winterwear, athleisure, kids' wear and home textiles
- Cotton products currently contribute approximately 55% of total revenue, anchoring the mix while newer categories scale
- Independent growth momentum in the specific sub-segments the Company has entered — footwear and athleisure — giving multiple separately expanding demand pools and reducing dependency on any single category or season
- Sustained high-growth phase in India's D2C and online fashion retail channels, with quick-commerce emerging as a meaningful new layer within online retail rather than a niche add-on; online net sales grew 38% year-on-year in FY26
- Deepening online penetration across smaller cities and broadening quick-commerce adoption beyond metro markets leaves a long runway in scaling digital channels and extending reach into geographies where physical distribution remains thin
- Temporary relief on input costs from the government's suspension of customs duty on cotton imports, at a time when cotton remains the dominant input for the largest product segment
- Government policy support for textiles — India-UK CETA and a reduced US reciprocal tariff (down to 18% from 50%), the concluded India-EU FTA negotiations (January 2026), INR 10,683 crore allocated under the textiles PLI scheme, seven operational PM MITRA parks backed by an INR 4,445 crore outlay, and GST 2.0 rationalisation cutting mass-market garment rates (up to INR 2,500) from 12% to 5%
- Macro backdrop: RBI projects India to grow approximately 6.6% in FY2026-27, a moderation from FY2025-26, with inflation contained (CPI approximately 3.4% in March 2026) and the repo rate at 5.25% in June 2026
- Debt-free on long-term borrowings with a CRISIL AA- long-term and A1+ short-term rating, giving liquidity and capital resources management believes sufficient for expected working capital needs

currentContext.expansion: Monte Carlo's expansion in FY26 was retail-footprint and channel led rather than plant led. The Company operates two state-of-the-art integrated manufacturing facilities in Ludhiana, Punjab (the Notice-of-AGM 'Works' listing names four Ludhiana sites: G.T. Road Sherpur; 231 Industrial Area-A; Plot No. 425 & 427 near Textile Colony; and B-XXX-1781/784, Old C-12, Phase V, Focal Point), supported by an in-house design team of 26+ professionals producing approximately 900 SKUs per month. It manufactures 100% of its woollen clothing and approximately 70% of its cotton garments in-house, with the remaining approximately 30% (home textiles, footwear and poly-blend products) outsourced to third-party manufacturers. As part of its FY27 growth strategy the Company plans to further modernise its manufacturing facilities and warehousing infrastructure and streamline business processes to support its expanding product portfolio. Retail expansion is the principal capacity build-out: during FY26 the network reached 497 Exclusive Brand Outlets (341 FOFO and 156 COCO), 1,615 Multi-Brand Outlets, 891 National Chain Store counters and 578 Shop-in-Shop/NCS outlets, with 26 net new EBOs added during the year. Going forward the Company intends to accelerate retail expansion through the asset-light FOFO model, targeting 40-45 Exclusive Brand Outlets annually (the Directors' Report states the addition of 40-50 new stores every year), while deepening North and East India and accelerating into the Southern and Western regions. New channels added in FY26 include entry into direct international e-commerce via the overseas platforms Joom.com and Stylishop.com, quick-commerce partnerships with Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto enabling deliveries within 30 minutes in select markets, and a strategic collaboration with Salesforce for digital transformation. On the corporate structure side the Company incorporated MCFL Energy Projects Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary on 19 January 2026 to undertake business in renewable energy and allied activities. No rupee capex quantum was disclosed: the capital-commitments named disclosure in this bundle carries only cross-references to note 34 and no figure.

thesis (one-liner): Monte Carlo is executing a de-seasonalization story — historically winter-wear-dependent, now near-50/50 winter vs summer (non-winter) revenue — while delivering on stated annual guidance (FY26: 16% revenue growth vs 15% guided), turning Q4 (a seasonally weak/return quarter) profitable after ~3 years, and adding optionality via footwear, home textiles, online/quick-commerce and a non-core solar IPP.
scorecard (yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 (full year) | YoY note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ~INR 280 cr | INR 1,276 cr | Q4 +36% YoY; FY +16% YoY (vs ~15% guided) |
| EBITDA | INR 26 cr | ~INR 227 cr | Q4 +353% YoY; FY +22% YoY |
| EBITDA margin | 9.2% (Q4) | 17.81% (ex-other income); ~20% incl. other income | FY margin met ~20% guidance (incl. other income) |
| PAT (reported) | INR 5 cr | INR 112 cr | Q4 swung from a LOSS of INR 10 cr LY to +INR 5 cr; FY PAT +38% YoY |
| PAT margin | 1.78% (Q4) | 8.79% (FY) | — |
| Gross margin | n/d (not explicitly given) | n/d | — |
| SSSG | n/d (not disclosed) | Volume +12% (annual); Q4 volume +~18–20% (mgmt estimate) | Growth from summer-category penetration + winter-loyalty crossover into summer |
| Store count (EBO) | — | 497 net (from 471), +26 NET / +43 gross | One-off correction: ~14–15 unprofitable stores closed last yr |
| Net cash | Net-cash / surplus (pays dividend, funds solar equity from cash) | — | INR 20/sh dividend declared FY26 |

**SEASONALITY CALL-OUT:** Winter-heavy business. Q3 is "very, very heavy"; **Q1 = only ~12–13% of annual revenue** because winter returns flow back in Apr–May AND primary sales are low. Returns split between Q4 and Q1, majority in Q1. FY26 mix: **Winter wear 45% · Non-winter/summer 42% · Textile ~10.2% · Accessories+footwear ~2%** — summer now nearly equal to winter.

**INVENTORY / RETURN POLICY CALL-OUT:** Full-year **returns rose to 17% (vs 15% LY)** of gross sales; **discounts FELL to 9.44% (vs 10.16% LY)** — lower discounting (not lower returns) drove the margin/profit improvement. **Inventory days fell to 144 (vs 169 LY)**; inventory value ~INR 570 cr. Mgmt says channel/store inventory is "very comfortable." As more business shifts to SIS / LFS / online (end-sale recognition, stock held at channel partners' accounts), inventory level unlikely to fall further.
guidance (critical):
- **FY27 revenue: explicit annual guidance DEFERRED to Q2 FY27 concall** (cited geopolitical/oil-inflation uncertainty). Firm directional commitment: **"double-digit growth is definitely on the cards"** for FY27; mgmt "more confident than last year" as all categories firing.
- **SSSG:** not guided as a number.
- **Store adds: 40–45 EBOs gross in FY27** (Western & Southern focus); could go to ~50. Net ≈ ~90% of gross (no further store-closure correction expected — that was a one-off in FY26).
- **Cotton vs woollen mix:** summer/non-winter to keep outgrowing winter ("9 months of summer," tropical-country thesis); summer expected to surpass winter over time.
- **Margin:** target **~20% EBITDA incl. other income** (achieved FY26); expect to stay in this range. Raw-material (cotton + wool) hikes fully covered — 7–8% price hike taken pre-trade-show; pass-through is immediate, no margin impact expected.
- **Home textile:** FY27 contribution guided up to **13–14% of revenue** (FY26 ~12%).
pipeline (store rollout):
- 40–45 EBOs/yr; stores 500–1,000 sq ft typical, average 1,000–1,500 sq ft (range 650 to 2,500). Western & Southern India emphasis.
- Cloak & Decker EBOs: +2 in Q4 → 24 total stores.
- ~50 large (>2,000 sq ft) stores carry home + footwear; ~30–35 larger EBOs being retrofitted to house footwear.
- Example unit economics: Noida Mall of India store, 650 sq ft → INR 4 cr sales (high-footfall locations prioritized over size).
segment / channel:
- **Categories (FY26 mix):** Winter 45% · Non-winter/summer 42% · Home textile 10.2% · Accessories+footwear 2%.
- **Rock.it** (summer/youth brand): +86% gross-sales growth FY26.
- **Footwear:** +149% gross sales FY26 (small base); targeting to DOUBLE turnover FY27; primarily online, experimenting offline (~15 Reliance LFS + 30–35 retrofitted EBOs).
- **Home textile:** robust growth, healthy demand; FY27 contribution → 13–14%.
- **Kidswear:** ~INR 110 cr run-rate (up from ~INR 100 cr).
- **Online:** net sales +38% FY26 (own website + portals like AJIO, Myntra; SOR/marketplace/outright mix). Online margins kept in line with other channels ("never want to bleed money online").
- **Quick-commerce:** Blinkit (Delhi NCR), Swiggy (Bangalore dark stores), Zepto onboarded, BigBasket in final talks — outright model, 30-min express delivery; geographic placement decided by the q-comm buyer.
- **Exports:** Middle East — only ~2,500–3,000 pcs (online, experimental); 70% sold in secondary market; repeat orders delayed 2–3 months due to Middle East uncertainty. Also onboarded Joom.com & Stylishop.com for overseas e-comm.
- **Channel margins:** vary by channel (MBO/SIS carry agency+distributor cost; LFS heavy manpower; franchised EBOs low pressure; factory outlets least margin), but total expenditure per vertical within ±4–5%.
growth / optionality:
- **De-seasonalization:** summer/non-winter (42%) approaching winter (45%); driven by category penetration across regions + winter-loyal customers crossing into summer purchases at EBOs.
- **Footwear** doubling potential; **home textile** scaling; **kidswear** & accessories growing with store count.
- **Online + quick-commerce** ecosystem build-out; Salesforce digital-transformation partnership for loyalty/CX.
- **Solar IPP (non-core):** ~40 MW PPA with MP govt (35 MW AC, ~30% overload → 43–45 MW); PPA tariff INR 2.79/unit; non-DCR modules (one of last tenders eligible; ~INR 1.25 cr/MW cheaper than DCR but NOT eligible for INR 1.05 cr/MW CFA subsidy). Capex INR 130–140 cr; ~75% debt / 25% equity. Revenue ~INR 15–16 cr/yr, ~90% net operating margin (O&M ~10%); projected IRR 15–16% over 25 yrs. Billing to start this FY; full operation within ~12 months. Exploring further IPP / BESS projects (IPP model, lease land, won't pursue IRR < 15–17%).
margins & cost:
- FY26 EBITDA margin 17.81% (ex-other income) / ~20% (incl. other income); maintained.
- Lower discounting (9.44% vs 10.16%) + adequate Q3 provisioning + summer-sales jump → Q4 turned profitable / profitability improvement.
- Raw-material (cotton, wool) inflation fully hedged pre-trade-show; immediate price pass-through; 7–8% hike taken.
capex:
- Apparel/manufacturing capex: "normal range" INR 10–15 cr/yr (no major expansion — 85% of production OUTSOURCED across India vendors; prefer outsourcing for incremental volume).
- Solar IPP capex: INR 130–140 cr (~75% debt-funded; ~25% equity from internal cash).
capital allocation:
- **Dividend:** INR 20/share declared for FY26 (regular dividend payer).
- Surplus cash → solar equity portion + future BESS/solar projects (only if IRR > 15–17%).
- **Buyback:** investor requested (share price "languishing," low multiple vs peers); mgmt will pass suggestion to board — no commitment.
- Net-cash/surplus position.
risks:
- **Winter dependence:** still 45% of revenue; weak winter / warm-winter season is the structural risk. Q1 structurally weak (~12–13% of annual revenue) due to winter returns.
- **Demand / macro:** petrol/diesel/LPG-driven inflation could defer discretionary apparel spend; geopolitical tension is the named overhang (reason guidance deferred to Q2).
- **Inventory:** ~INR 570 cr inventory; 144 days (improved but still high); unlikely to reduce further given channel-held stock model.
- **Returns:** elevated at 17% of gross sales (up from 15%).
- **Solar execution:** highly leveraged (75% debt), commissioning/vendor finalization pending, IRR sensitivity; non-core distraction risk.
- **Export:** Middle East orders stalled on regional uncertainty.
- **Competition:** fast-fashion (Zara, Shein) — mgmt dismisses (present in India 10–15 yrs already; relies on own design USP + large market).
management tone: Confident and execution-focused. Repeatedly emphasized track record of meeting annual guidance (guided 15%, delivered 16%; ~20% EBITDA met). Deliberately conservative on FY27 quantitative guidance — explicitly deferred to Q2 citing geopolitical/oil uncertainty, while firmly committing to "double-digit growth." Notably more candid on energy diversification (Rishabh Oswal). Declines quarter-by-quarter guidance on principle (seasonality).
non-obvious points:
- Margin beat driven by LOWER DISCOUNTS, not lower returns — returns actually ROSE to 17%. Investors initially assumed lower returns helped; mgmt corrected.
- Inventory won't structurally fall because shift to SIS/LFS/online means stock sits in channel partners' accounts (only end-sales recognized).
- Solar revenue (~INR 15–16 cr) is OVER AND ABOVE / outside the standalone apparel guidance — don't double-count.
- One-off FY26 store correction (~14–15 closures) masks underlying ~43 gross store adds; muddies the net-26 figure vs 40–45 guidance.
- Q1 is only ~12–13% of full-year revenue — a weak Q1 print is structural, not a red flag.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Structural transformation of India's textile and apparel industry supported by strong domestic consumption, rising organised retail penetration, increasing digitalisation and expanding global sourcing opportunities
- Premiumisation of the Indian fashion market driven by rising disposable incomes, greater brand awareness and consumer preference for quality and differentiated product offerings; per Deloitte, the mid-premium band (INR 3,500-7,000) is projected to grow strongly and premium apparel faster still
- Shift towards branded and organised retail, omnichannel commerce and products offering greater comfort, functionality and sustainability, creating opportunities across apparel, winterwear, athleisure, kids' wear and home textiles
- Cotton products currently contribute approximately 55% of total revenue, anchoring the mix while newer categories scale
- Independent growth momentum in the specific sub-segments the Company has entered — footwear and athleisure — giving multiple separately expanding demand pools and reducing dependency on any single category or season
- Sustained high-growth phase in India's D2C and online fashion retail channels, with quick-commerce emerging as a meaningful new layer within online retail rather than a niche add-on; online net sales grew 38% year-on-year in FY26
- Deepening online penetration across smaller cities and broadening quick-commerce adoption beyond metro markets leaves a long runway in scaling digital channels and extending reach into geographies where physical distribution remains thin
- Temporary relief on input costs from the government's suspension of customs duty on cotton imports, at a time when cotton remains the dominant input for the largest product segment
- Government policy support for textiles — India-UK CETA and a reduced US reciprocal tariff (down to 18% from 50%), the concluded India-EU FTA negotiations (January 2026), INR 10,683 crore allocated under the textiles PLI scheme, seven operational PM MITRA parks backed by an INR 4,445 crore outlay, and GST 2.0 rationalisation cutting mass-market garment rates (up to INR 2,500) from 12% to 5%
- Macro backdrop: RBI projects India to grow approximately 6.6% in FY2026-27, a moderation from FY2025-26, with inflation contained (CPI approximately 3.4% in March 2026) and the repo rate at 5.25% in June 2026

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Monte Carlo's expansion in FY26 was retail-footprint and channel led rather than plant led. The Company operates two state-of-the-art integrated manufacturing facilities in Ludhiana, Punjab (the Notice-of-AGM 'Works' listing names four Ludhiana sites: G.T. Road Sherpur; 231 Industrial Area-A; Plot No. 425 & 427 near Textile Colony; and B-XXX-1781/784, Old C-12, Phase V, Focal Point), supported by an in-house design team of 26+ professionals producing approximately 900 SKUs per month. It manufactures 100% of its woollen clothing and approximately 70% of its cotton garments in-house, with the remaining approximately 30% (home textiles, footwear and poly-blend products) outsourced to third-party manufacturers. As part of its FY27 growth strategy the Company plans to further modernise its manufacturing facilities and warehousing infrastructure and streamline business processes to support its expanding product portfolio. Retail expansion is the principal capacity build-out: during FY26 the network reached 497 Exclusive Brand Outlets (341 FOFO and 156 COCO), 1,615 Multi-Brand Outlets, 891 National Chain Store counters and 578 Shop-in-Shop/NCS outlets, with 26 net new EBOs added during the year. Going forward the Company intends to accelerate retail expansion through the asset-light FOFO model, targeting 40-45 Exclusive Brand Outlets annually (the Directors' Report states the addition of 40-50 new stores every year), while deepening North and East India and accelerating into the Southern and Western regions. New channels added in FY26 include entry into direct international e-commerce via the overseas platforms Joom.com and Stylishop.com, quick-commerce partnerships with Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto enabling deliveries within 30 minutes in select markets, and a strategic collaboration with Salesforce for digital transformation. On the corporate structure side the Company incorporated MCFL Energy Projects Private Limited as a wholly-owned subsidiary on 19 January 2026 to undertake business in renewable energy and allied activities. No rupee capex quantum was disclosed: the capital-commitments named disclosure in this bundle carries only cross-references to note 34 and no figure.

themes.title: Quick-commerce, omnichannel & retail expansion
themes.need: Quick-commerce and value retail are the structural growth engine, and Q1FY27 rewrote the unit-economics model. ETERNAL raised Blinkit's steady-state margin from a 5-6% range to ~6% and set a first-ever 4% GAAP EBIT margin target (after ESOP and depreciation) while capex per store went from INR 1cr to INR 2.5cr (+150%) with NOV/store/day up only 60% and net working capital improving 18 to 14 days - so margin can now drift DOWN while ROCE improves. Growth also decoupled from spend: Blinkit orders +21% QoQ with MTUs above 30mn achieved on LOWER marketing spend and fewer store adds, and management called Q1 the peak of competitive intensity to date. VMM did INR 3,727cr (+18.7%) on 10% SSSG with gross margin up to 28.7% driven by lower promotional spend rather than price hikes, validated a small-format store at the same revenue/sq ft and 'pretty much the same' ROCE as large format (a ~3,000-store national opportunity), and found 20% of its quick-commerce customers had never shopped a Vishal store. SHOPERSTOP swung PAT positive (+INR 5cr vs -INR 4cr) and raised FY27 LFL guidance from 5% to ~6%; ARVINDFASN lifted gross margin 90bps to 56.7% on full-price sell-through with direct channels now 62% of sales; MEESHO cut cost per delivered order ~INR 1 QoQ despite the May fuel hike. DMART/V2RETAIL/PATELRMART on value retail; TRENT-tier branded retail via ABFRL/METROBRAND/BATAINDIA/REDTAPE.
